title: More than Memes: A Multimodal Topic Modeling Approach to Conspiracy Theories on Telegram
venue: Proceedings of the International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media (ICWSM 2025)
subcategory: text, image and text-image BERTopic comparison
task: Comparing unimodal and multimodal topic models on conspiracy-theory content
problem: Research on conspiracy content is mostly text-based and lacks ways to compare topic models across modalities.
architecture: BERTopic with paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 for text and clip-ViT-B-32 for images and averaged text-image embeddings; UMAP + HDBSCAN defaults; image topics represented through vit-gpt2 captions; min topic size 10/20/50 compared; topic symmetry and intersection analysis across modalities; LLM-based topic annotation.
llm_or_encoder: paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2; CLIP ViT-B-32; vit-gpt2 image captioning; a generative LLM for annotation

datasets.name: German-language Telegram channels
datasets.details: 40,110 messages from 571 channels (October 2023) after deduplication; text 36,717, image 34,850, multimodal 31,982 subcorpora; November 2024 data for transfer

baselines: text-only vs image-only vs multimodal BERTopic
key_results: With min topic size 20: 167 text topics (41.4% outliers), 157 image topics (35.3%), 146 multimodal topics (35.7%).
Israel-Gaza dominates in October 2023: 36.2% of text, 12.9% of image and 16.7% of multimodal messages; symmetry lowest between text and image models.
strengths: Shows image and multimodal topics capture content missed by text-only models (e.g. screenshots, protest images).
Checks temporal transfer with a second data period.

limitations.text: CLIP is not tuned for noisy user content; no standard evaluation metrics for BERTopic, so quality judgements are subjective; period selection may bias topics.
